full_judgment:
4. During trial the plaintiff adduced 3 witnesses while the defendant adduced 1 witness. The plaintiff also produced documentary evidence and the defendant adduced copies of the SA khatian and RS Khatian. The trial Court after hearing the parties and considering the materials on record as well as evidence, both the oral and documentary evidence, dismissed the suit. 

 6. Mr Abul Hashem, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal and the Court of appeal below while passing the impugned judgment did not advert to the finding and observation arrived at by the trial Court and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He submits that admittedly the suit is barred by section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also the plaintiff failed to prefer any appeal against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.l51 of 1975. He further submits that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 11 0 of 1975 is not binding upon the petitioners because there had been defect of parties in the suit and admittedly SA and RS Khatian were prepared in the name of the defendant-petitioner Government. In such circumstances, the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court is liable to be set aside for the ends of justice.
